title: What is a {{term:fraction}}?
summary: Split one whole into equal parts and use a fraction to say how many parts you took.
guide: Each bar is one whole, like a bar of chocolate. It is split into equal parts.
Tap a part to shade it. Tap it again to unshade it.

In the fraction {{frac:3/4}}, the bottom number (the {{term:denominator}}) says how many equal parts the whole is split into, and the top number (the {{term:numerator}}) says how many parts are shaded.

one-quarter.title: One quarter
one-quarter.prompt: This bar is split into 4 equal parts. Shade {{frac:1/4}} of the bar.
one-quarter.hint: The bottom number is 4: four equal parts. The top number is 1, so shade just one part.
one-quarter.success: Well done! One of four equal parts is {{frac:1/4}}.
one-quarter.why: If the bar were split into 4 unequal parts, would shading one part still be {{frac:1/4}}? Why?
one-quarter.model: No. {{frac:1/4}} means one of 4 equal parts. If the parts are different sizes, one part could be more or less than a quarter of the whole.

feedback.too-big: That's too much. {{frac:1/4}} is just 1 part out of 4.
feedback.empty: You haven't shaded any parts yet. Tap one part.

three-quarters.title: Three quarters
three-quarters.hint: The top number is 3: shade three of the four equal parts.
three-quarters.success: That's right! Three of four equal parts.
three-quarters.why: What fraction of the bar is not shaded? How do you know?
three-quarters.model: {{frac:1/4}} is not shaded, because 3 of the 4 equal parts are shaded and 1 part is left.

feedback.too-small: Not enough. {{frac:3/4}} means 3 parts out of 4.
feedback.too-big: Too much. {{frac:3/4}} is 3 parts, not all 4.

name-it.title: Name the fraction
name-it.prompt: What fraction of this bar is shaded? Write the numerator and the denominator.
name-it.hint: First count how many equal parts the bar has (the denominator). Then count the shaded parts (the numerator).
name-it.success: Well done! 2 of 5 equal parts is {{frac:2/5}}.
name-it.why: Why is the denominator of this fraction 5?
name-it.model: Because the bar is split into 5 equal parts. The denominator is always the number of equal parts in the whole.

feedback.wrong-denominator: Count the equal parts of the bar again; that's the denominator.
feedback.too-big: Count the top or bottom number again. The numerator is the number of shaded parts.
feedback.too-small: Count the top or bottom number again. The numerator is the number of shaded parts.

make-sixths.title: Make your own parts
make-sixths.prompt: Use the + and − buttons to split the bar into the right number of equal parts, then shade {{frac:1/6}} of it.
make-sixths.hint: {{frac:1/6}} means 6 equal parts. Split the bar into 6 and shade one.
make-sixths.success: Great! The bar has 6 equal parts and one is shaded: {{frac:1/6}}.
make-sixths.why: Which is bigger, {{frac:1/6}} or {{frac:1/2}}? Use the bar to explain.
make-sixths.model: {{frac:1/2}} is bigger. When you split a whole into more parts, each part gets smaller, so one part out of 6 is smaller than one part out of 2.

feedback.wrong-denominator: Right amount, but split the bar into exactly 6 parts.
feedback.too-big: Either the bar doesn't have 6 parts yet, or more than one part is shaded.
